summary: You take two RELIGST courses numbered 1-99 (at most one Introductory Seminar), three numbered 100-289 (one at the 200 level) and more RELIGST courses to reach 28 units, all letter graded, with at most one directed reading course (RELIGST 199). An approved language course or other exception is moved in by hand, and the spread across religious traditions is checked by hand.

QTGc8bH5.why: "Two courses (3-5 units each) from courses numbered RELIGST 1-99, only one of which may be an Introductory Seminar." The Introductory Seminars are the department's N and Q courses.

xHXFBHOT.why: "Three courses (4-5 units each) from courses numbered RELIGST 100-289, of which at least one must be at the 200-level."

lq5XU1HU.why: "The remainder of the coursework needed to bring the total Religious Studies unit count to 28 is chosen in consultation with the student’s minor advisor according to interest." Five courses reach at most 25 units, so at least one more RELIGST course; the block floor checks the 28. Policies: "One course in directed reading (course Individual Work) may be counted towards the minor." Individual Work is RELIGST 199.

program.why: Grading: "No courses may be taken for the S/NC or CR/NC grade."

totals.why: Grading: "No courses may be taken for the S/NC or CR/NC grade." This also keeps out courses offered only S/NC.

add.why: Policies: "With the approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies, one language course relating to the student's program of study ... may be counted towards the minor." and "All units must be in Religious Studies courses unless an exception is made by the Director of Undergraduate Studies."
